 # Research-team experiment catalogue
 
+- [Online input relationships with a frozen-parent residual head](online-relationships-20261022/README.md) — [draft PR #38](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/38), a focused 12-readout-fit proposal for H-ONLINE-RELATIONSHIPS-20261022-R1 / E-ONLINE-RELATIONSHIPS-20261022-R1. Root has admitted the panel; the dated snapshot has zero completed fits and quality grading is pending. The executed source freeze is root commit `17470a770f2a6aa25be232c017bff45b5d56ad97`; the packet/recipe commit is `33c6e33830a89187aaaf08116850864250feed56`. This integration preserves four canonical dependency differences, so its PR branch is not the executed checkout and exact preflight refuses it. See the packet's [publication receipt](online-relationships-20261022/PUBLICATION_RECEIPT_R1.json).
+
 - [PR #28: teacher-transfer-frontier](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/28) — reviewed proposal with CP30 recipe; packet lives on its experiment branch, no fits or ready launch.
 - [PR #29: teacher-representation-hints](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/29) — reviewed proposal with CP30 recipe; packet lives on its experiment branch, no fits or ready launch.

+# Online input relationships with a frozen-parent residual head
+
+1. **Status, lineage and owner.** This is the focused draft for H-ONLINE-RELATIONSHIPS-20261022-R1 / E-ONLINE-RELATIONSHIPS-20261022-R1. The feature state, readout, full-cache delivery and independent grader are implemented and source-reviewed. Root admitted twelve new readout fits; the panel is still running and has no quality grade. The executed source freeze is `17470a770f2a6aa25be232c017bff45b5d56ad97` on `experiment/next-cycle-recovery-20261021`; reproducible recipe/admission/launcher packet is committed at root `33c6e33830a89187aaaf08116850864250feed56`. This PR is a narrow overlay on `research-team` and was not the executed checkout. Its four preserved canonical dependency files differ from the frozen run hashes, so the exact source preflight rejects this PR head. No parity, quality or full-FP32 execution claim is made for PR HEAD. Root owns admission and delivery; the independent grader owns artifact validation and scoring.
+
+2. **Why it should work.** A causal state of input-only forecasts, pre-update innovations and slopes may reveal residual structure that the frozen parent misses. Arm A adapts the mean only and fixes slope to zero; B adapts slope/intercept through row 98, then freezes; C continues updating slope/intercept. C−A asks whether relationships add value beyond mean adaptation; C−B asks whether continued adaptation helps after warmup. A lower input-prediction loss alone is not evidence of endpoint value. The strongest alternatives are ordinary calibration, fold/seed variation and a learned residual distribution that does not transfer from in-sample parent predictions.
+
+3. **Compute advantage.** Each candidate is a 64-unit tanh residual readout on top of a reused frozen parent endpoint. This screen adds no GRU or teacher fits and does not train a new backbone. The resource decision is an inclusive 8,311.440-second CPU panel within the 9,000-second online ceiling, including cache/I/O and separate grading reserves; it preserves the 43,200-second production reserve. B300 is deferred. If the small-head endpoint earns further work, the next step is a targeted, source-qualified follow-up or native-serving test; no scale law, public-score gain or production benefit is assumed.
+
+4. **Frozen comparison.** The admitted immutable recipe uses 419 inputs: canonical `standard211` plus matured i0 changes, forecasts, pre-update errors and slopes (52 each). The online state uses raw observations only, updates causally, resets at each sequence, and never reads labels, scoring masks or prediction flags. Separate lag-1 and lag-16 panels are used. The residual is `parent + 0.1 * head`; head output initializes to zero. All arms use strict FP32 with autocast and TF32 off; canonical fitting row weights and WMSE; AdamW at 0.001, weight decay 0.01, gradient clip 1, batches of 8,192 rows, three epochs and fixed epoch-2 checkpoint selection. Fit-only standardization uses a 0.001 standard-deviation floor and clips standardized differences to ±8. Means/covariance start at zero, input variance at one; slope ridge is 0.1 and the state half-life is 512. The exact optimizer, target, parent, sequence and reset contracts are pinned in `EXECUTION_RECIPE_R1.json` and `PANEL_ADMISSION_R1.json`.
+
+5. **Bounded fitting panel.** The explicit lag amendment admits two matched panels: folds 0 and 1 with fitting seeds 1001 and 1002, respectively; each cell has arms A/B/C at lags 1 and 16. This is 4 new readout fits per arm, 2 per arm per lag, and 12 total new fits. Two exact fold-specific parent endpoints are reused across the arms/lags. There are zero new GRU fits, teacher fits or backbone/student fits. Each cell uses the recipe-pinned 10% source-qualified component sample and complete sequences. No additional follow-up fits are included in this admission.
+
+6. **Validation and uncertainty.** The unchanged official metric is `global_wp_clip2_v1`, with its fixed scored/prediction mask, ±2 clipping and original clipped-label magnitude weights. The grader evaluates both targets and four fixed position bins on both source-qualified folds. Planned primary contrasts are C−A, C−B and each arm against its matched parent within each fold/lag; lag-16 minus lag-1 per arm/cell is secondary (26 contrasts total). The paired dependency-component bootstrap is conditional on these fixed endpoints and excludes fitting variation and public transfer. Both folds are exposed; the two fold/seed cells confound those axes and cannot estimate training variance or establish significance. Report every paired delta and interval; do not promote on an isolated positive component interval.
+
+7. **Leakage and coverage.** Online updates are past-only and use raw inputs, not targets, masks or request/score flags. Unavailable backward differences are zero placeholders and excluded from fitting standardization until mature; warmup spans rows 16–98, with 82 real lag-1 and 67 real lag-16 regressor pairs. Sequence state resets on boundaries. Exact cache headers, source-qualified membership, parent normalization and coverage are checked before grading. Parent training predictions are in-sample rather than OOF, so the learned residual distribution may differ on held-out components. All folds used here are exposed; this screen does not create a fresh holdout.
+
+8. **Decision-changing result.** A coherent endpoint improvement for C over A and B supports continued relationship adaptation in this readout; improvement only over A is consistent with calibration rather than ongoing adaptation. An input-loss improvement without official endpoint value earns no expansion. The screen is small, so mixed or imprecise results remain uncertain and can justify only a bounded information-seeking follow-up when its expected value exceeds its cost. Negative evidence narrows this exact readout and panel; it does not reject online learning generally. Any release also requires actual native endpoint quality and runtime while preserving `PredictionModel.predict`; neither is established here.

+"""Grade a root-admitted online relationship panel after validating every artifact."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import sys
+from datetime import UTC, datetime
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any  # JSON metadata is validated at runtime.
+
+from online_relationship_grade_contract import (
+    ARMS,
+    CandidateArtifacts,
+    ParentCacheArtifacts,
+    _resolve,
+    read_json,
+    validate_recipe,
+)
+from online_relationship_grade_core import (
+    BOOTSTRAP_DRAWS,
+    BOOTSTRAP_SEED,
+    sha256_file,
+)
+from online_relationship_grade_outputs import verify_candidate
+from online_relationship_grade_parent import verify_parent_cache
+from online_relationship_grade_scoring import grade_fold
+from online_relationship_grade_targets import load_targets
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+
+
+def _validate_artifacts(
+    recipe_path: Path, recipe_sha: str
+) -> tuple[
+    dict[str, Any],
+    dict[int, ParentCacheArtifacts],
+    dict[tuple[int, int, str], CandidateArtifacts],
+    dict[int, dict[str, Any]],
+]:
+    recipe, actual_recipe_sha = validate_recipe(recipe_path, ROOT, recipe_sha)
+    folds = {int(record["fold"]): record for record in recipe["folds"]}
+    parent_caches = {
+        fold_id: verify_parent_cache(ROOT, recipe, actual_recipe_sha, fold, recipe_path)
+        for fold_id, fold in folds.items()
+    }
+    subsets = {
+        fold_id: read_json(_resolve(ROOT, fold["subset"]["path"]))
+        for fold_id, fold in folds.items()
+    }
+    candidates: dict[tuple[int, int, str], CandidateArtifacts] = {}
+    for cell in recipe["cells"]:
+        fold_id = int(cell["fold"])
+        key = (fold_id, int(cell["lag"]), str(cell["arm"]))
+        if key in candidates:
+            raise ValueError(f"duplicate candidate cell {key}")
+        candidates[key] = verify_candidate(
+            ROOT,
+            recipe,
+            recipe_path,
+            actual_recipe_sha,
+            folds[fold_id],
+            cell,
+            subsets[fold_id],
+            parent_caches[fold_id],
+        )
+    if len(parent_caches) != 2 or len(candidates) != 12:
+        raise ValueError("all two parent endpoints and twelve candidates are required")

+
+
+def _validate_panel_consistency(
+    parent_caches: dict[int, ParentCacheArtifacts],
+    candidates: dict[tuple[int, int, str], CandidateArtifacts],
+) -> None:
+    """Require each matched fold/lag panel to share all source and membership inputs."""
+    all_candidate_sources: set[str] = set()
+    for fold_id, parent in parent_caches.items():
+        fold_rows = [value.identity for key, value in candidates.items() if key[0] == fold_id]
+        if len(fold_rows) != 6:
+            raise ValueError(f"F{fold_id} does not have all six lag/arm outputs")
+        parent_sha = parent.identity["evaluation_prediction_sidecar_sha256"]
+        if any(row["parent_cache_manifest_sha256"] != parent_sha for row in fold_rows):
+            raise ValueError(f"F{fold_id} candidates do not share the verified parent cache")
+        if len({row["fit_membership_sha256"] for row in fold_rows}) != 1:
+            raise ValueError(f"F{fold_id} candidates use different fit memberships")
+        source_ids = {json.dumps(row["source_sha256"], sort_keys=True) for row in fold_rows}
+        if len(source_ids) != 1:
+            raise ValueError(f"F{fold_id} candidates use different source-code identities")
+        all_candidate_sources.update(source_ids)
+        if len({row["evaluation_membership_sha256"] for row in fold_rows}) != 1:
+            raise ValueError(f"F{fold_id} candidates use different evaluation order")

+            }
+            if len(normalizers) != 1:

+    if (
+        len(
+            {
+                json.dumps(value.identity["cache_source_sha256"], sort_keys=True)
+                for value in parent_caches.values()
+            }
+        )
+        != 1
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("parent-cache builder source identity differs across folds")
+
+
+def _recheck_output_files(
+    parents: dict[int, ParentCacheArtifacts],
+    candidates: dict[tuple[int, int, str], CandidateArtifacts],
+) -> None:

+            ("checkpoint_path", "checkpoint_sha256"),

+                raise ValueError(f"{identity['run']}: candidate changed after validation")
+
+

+    parser.add_argument("--recipe-sha256", required=True)

+        endpoint_report, contrasts = grade_fold(

+        )
+        fold_reports.append(endpoint_report)
+        contrast_reports.extend(contrasts)

+        raise AssertionError("panel grading did not produce exactly 26 fold-local contrasts")

+    grader_sources = (
+        Path(__file__),
+        Path(__file__).with_name("online_relationship_grade_contract.py"),
+        Path(__file__).with_name("online_relationship_grade_parent.py"),
+        Path(__file__).with_name("online_relationship_grade_cache.py"),

+        Path(__file__).with_name("online_relationship_grade_core.py"),
+        Path(__file__).with_name("online_relationship_grade_scoring.py"),
+        Path(__file__).with_name("online_relationship_grade_targets.py"),
+        ROOT / "scripts/grade_prediction_bank.py",
+        ROOT / "src/wnn/evaluation.py",
+        ROOT / "src/wnn/gmetric.py",
+        ROOT / "src/wnn/splits.py",
+        ROOT / "src/wnn/training/membership.py",
+    )
+    report = {
+        "schema": "wnn.online-relationships-grade.v1",
+        "created_utc": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(),
+        "recipe": {"path": str(recipe_path), "sha256": args.recipe_sha256},

+        },
+        "metric": "global_wp_clip2_v1",
+        "targets": {
+            "path": recipe["target_cache"]["path"],
+            "sha256": recipe["target_cache"]["sha256"],

+        "contrast_count": len(contrast_reports),
+        "folds": fold_reports,
+        "contrasts": contrast_reports,
+        "interpretation": {
+            "fold_seed_confounding": "F0 and seed1001 versus F1 and seed1002 are separate cells; no pooled seed effect is estimated.",
+            "validation_exposure": "Both full validation folds were previously inspected and remain exposed development evidence.",
+            "fit_parent_scope": "Parent predictions on selected fitting groups are in-sample and are never graded as endpoints.",

+            "fixed_points": "Both target correlations and four fixed position-bin scores are point deltas for these fixed models.",

+    output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    with output_path.open("x", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
+        json.dump(report, stream, indent=2, allow_nan=False)
+        stream.write("\n")
+    print(json.dumps({"grade": str(output_path), "endpoints": 14, "contrasts": 26}))
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+"""Validate the exact sequence-cache headers, membership and source identities."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any  # JSON metadata is validated at runtime.
+
+import numpy as np
+from online_relationship_grade_contract import (
+    ROWS,
+    WIDTH,
+    _resolve,
+    _verify_source_hashes,
+    read_json,
+    row_refs_sha256,
+)
+from online_relationship_grade_core import npy_coverage, sha256_file
+
+
+def verify_sequence_cache(
+    root: Path,
+    split: dict[str, Any],
+    data_path: Path,
+    metadata_path: Path,
+    scope: str,
+    refs: list[dict[str, Any]],
+    recipe: dict[str, Any],
+    recipe_sha: str,
+    fold: dict[str, Any],
+    subset: dict[str, Any],
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    metadata = read_json(metadata_path)
+    fold_id = int(fold["fold"])
+    expected = {
+        "schema": "wnn.online-relationships.sequence-cache.v1",
+        "scope": scope,
+        "fold": fold_id,
+        "seed": int(fold["seed"]),
+        "recipe_id": recipe["recipe_id"],
+        "recipe_sha256": recipe_sha,
+        "split_manifest_sha256": fold["split_manifest_sha256"],
+        "subset_manifest_sha256": fold["subset"]["sha256"],
+        "subset_members_sha256": subset["selected_members_sha256"],
+        "row_refs": refs,
+        "membership_sha256": row_refs_sha256(refs),
+        "complete_membership": True,
+        "scope_label": scope,
+        "data_file": data_path.name,
+        "shape": [len(refs), ROWS, WIDTH],
+        "dtype": "<f4",
+    }
+    for key, value in expected.items():
+        if metadata.get(key) != value:
+            raise ValueError(f"F{fold_id} {scope} cache field {key} differs from the recipe")
+    if metadata.get("sampled_profile") is not False:
+        raise ValueError(f"F{fold_id} {scope} cache is a profile sample, not complete")
+    if metadata.get("split_manifest") != str(_resolve(root, fold["split_manifest"])):
+        raise ValueError(f"F{fold_id} {scope} cache names a different split manifest")
+    if metadata.get("subset_manifest") != fold["subset"]["path"]:
+        raise ValueError(f"F{fold_id} {scope} cache names a different fit subset")
+    if metadata.get("layout") != {
+        "raw": [0, 112],
+        "target": [112, 114],
+        "row_weight": [114, 115],
+        "parent_prediction": [115, 117],
+    }:
+        raise ValueError(f"F{fold_id} {scope} cache layout changed")
+    parent_identity = metadata.get("parent", {})
+    parent_recipe = fold["parent"]
+    expected_parent = {
+        "run": parent_recipe["run"],
+        "epoch": parent_recipe["epoch"],
+        "checkpoint": str(_resolve(root, parent_recipe["checkpoint"])),
+        "checkpoint_sha256": parent_recipe["checkpoint_sha256"],
+        "provenance": str(_resolve(root, parent_recipe["provenance"])),
+        "provenance_sha256": parent_recipe["provenance_sha256"],
+        "mean_sha256": parent_recipe["mean_identity"],
+        "std_sha256": parent_recipe["std_identity"],
+        "input_width": parent_recipe["input_width"],
+    }
+    if any(parent_identity.get(key) != value for key, value in expected_parent.items()):
+        raise ValueError(f"F{fold_id} {scope} cache parent identity differs from the recipe")
+    if metadata.get("propensity") is not None and scope != "in_sample_fit":
+        raise ValueError(f"F{fold_id} evaluation cache unexpectedly binds propensity outputs")
+    if scope == "in_sample_fit":
+        propensity = metadata.get("propensity", {})
+        expected_propensity = fold["canonical_propensity"]
+        if (
+            propensity.get("run") != expected_propensity["run"]
+            or propensity.get("checkpoint_sha256") != expected_propensity["checkpoint_sha256"]
+            or propensity.get("provenance_sha256") != expected_propensity["provenance_sha256"]
+            or propensity.get("precision")
+            != "FP32 CPU probabilities; no cached propensity rows reused"
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(f"F{fold_id} fit cache uses a different propensity ancestor")
+    coverage = npy_coverage(data_path)
+    if coverage["shape"] != expected["shape"] or coverage["dtype"] != "<f4":
+        raise ValueError(f"F{fold_id} {scope} NPY header differs from its frozen schema")
+    data_sha = sha256_file(data_path)
+    if metadata.get("data_sha256") != data_sha:
+        raise ValueError(f"F{fold_id} {scope} payload SHA256 differs from the sidecar")
+    _verify_parent_stats(fold, metadata)
+    _verify_dataset_identities(root, split, metadata)
+    _verify_source_hashes(root, metadata.get("source_sha256", {}))
+    required = {
+        "src/wnn/splits.py",
+        "src/wnn/training/membership.py",
+        "src/wnn/training/online_relationship_data.py",
+        "src/wnn/training/online_relationship_data_writer.py",
+        "src/wnn/training/online_relationship_cache.py",
+        "src/wnn/training/online_relationship_sources.py",
+        "src/wnn/training/online_relationship.py",
+        "src/wnn/training/online_relationship_fit.py",
+        "src/wnn/training/inputs.py",
+        "src/wnn/training/targets.py",
+        "src/wnn/training/models.py",
+        "src/wnn/training/evaluation.py",
+        "src/wnn/training/environment.py",
+        "src/wnn/data.py",
+        "src/wnn/features.py",
+        "src/wnn/propensity.py",
+        "src/wnn/online_relationship.py",
+        "src/wnn/online_relationship_numba.py",
+    }
+    if not required.issubset(metadata["source_sha256"]):
+        raise ValueError(f"F{fold_id} {scope} cache source map omits builder dependencies")
+    return {**metadata, "data_sha256": data_sha}
+
+
+def _verify_parent_stats(fold: dict[str, Any], metadata: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    parent = fold["parent"]
+    for name, identity in (("parent_mean", "mean_identity"), ("parent_std", "std_identity")):
+        values = np.asarray(metadata.get(name), dtype="<f4")
+        if values.shape != (211,) or not np.isfinite(values).all():
+            raise ValueError(f"F{fold['fold']} cache {name} must be a finite 211-vector")
+        digest = hashlib.sha256(values.tobytes()).hexdigest()
+        if digest != parent[identity]:
+            raise ValueError(f"F{fold['fold']} cache {name} differs from the frozen parent")
+        if name == "parent_std" and np.any(values <= 0):
+            raise ValueError(f"F{fold['fold']} cache parent std must be positive")
+
+
+def _verify_dataset_identities(root: Path, split: dict[str, Any], metadata: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """Require the cached train/valid Parquet metadata to match its split manifest."""
+    identity = metadata.get("source_datasets", {})
+    for name in ("train", "valid"):
+        record = identity.get("sources", {}).get(name)
+        if not isinstance(record, dict):
+            raise ValueError(f"parent cache lacks {name} dataset identity")
+        path = root / "datasets" / f"{name}.parquet"
+        stat = path.stat()
+        if (
+            record.get("path") != str(path)
+            or record.get("bytes") != stat.st_size
+            or record.get("mtime_ns") != stat.st_mtime_ns
+            or record.get("campaign_identity")
+            != split.get("sources", {}).get(f"datasets/{name}.parquet")
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(f"parent cache {name} dataset identity differs from the split")

+"""Frozen recipe and shared identity checks for the relationship grader."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any  # JSON metadata is validated at runtime.
+
+from online_relationship_grade_core import sha256_file
+
+ROWS = 20_000
+WIDTH = 117
+RAW_END = 112
+PARENT_START = 115
+PARENT_END = 117
+ARMS = ("A", "B", "C")
+LAGS = (1, 16)
+EXPECTED_CELLS = {(fold, lag, arm) for fold in (0, 1) for lag in LAGS for arm in ARMS}
+ROW_WEIGHT_CONTRACT = {
+    "mask_weight": False,
+    "prop_power": 2.0,
+    "prop_eps": 0.03,
+    "prop_cache": False,
+    "class_weight": None,
+    "valid_true_mask": 0.03,
+    "sync_free": False,
+    "since_weight": 0.0,
+    "since_floor": 0.1,
+    "episode_weight": 0.0,
+    "episode_floor": 0.1,
+}
+ADMITTED_RECIPE_STATUSES = {"admitted_for_execution", "admitted", "completed"}
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ParentCacheArtifacts:
+    """Verified mmap and source identities for one fold's parent endpoint."""
+
+    prediction: Any
+    identity: dict[str, Any]
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class CandidateArtifacts:
+    """Verified prediction mmap, sidecar and provenance identity for one cell."""
+
+    prediction: Any
+    identity: dict[str, Any]
+
+
+def read_json(path: Path, *, max_bytes: int = 5_000_000) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Read bounded UTF-8 JSON metadata and require an object root."""
+    size = path.stat().st_size
+    if size <= 0 or size > max_bytes:
+        raise ValueError(f"metadata size is invalid: {path}")
+    value = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    if not isinstance(value, dict):
+        raise ValueError(f"metadata root must be an object: {path}")
+    return value
+
+
+def row_refs_sha256(refs: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> str:
+    """Hash ordered, normalized source-qualified split and row-group references."""
+    normalized = [{"split": str(ref["split"]), "row_group": int(ref["row_group"])} for ref in refs]
+    raw = json.dumps(normalized, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode("ascii")
+    return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
+
+
+def validate_recipe(
+    recipe_path: Path, root: Path, expected_sha256: str
+) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], str]:
+    """Pin recipe bytes and require an admitted complete F0/F1 × lag × arm panel."""
+    recipe = read_json(recipe_path)
+    recipe_sha = sha256_file(recipe_path)
+    if recipe_sha != expected_sha256:
+        raise ValueError("recipe bytes differ from the supplied frozen recipe SHA256")
+    if recipe.get("schema") != "wnn.online-relationships.v1":
+        raise ValueError("unsupported online relationship recipe")
+    if recipe.get("experiment_id") != "E-ONLINE-RELATIONSHIPS-20261022-R1":
+        raise ValueError("unexpected online relationship experiment identity")
+    if recipe.get("status") not in ADMITTED_RECIPE_STATUSES:
+        raise ValueError("recipe is not root-admitted for quality grading")
+    cells = recipe.get("cells", [])
+    if recipe.get("admitted_new_fits") != 12 or len(cells) != 12:
+        raise ValueError("root has not admitted the complete 12-fit panel")
+    grid = {(int(cell["fold"]), int(cell["lag"]), str(cell["arm"])) for cell in cells}
+    if grid != EXPECTED_CELLS or len(grid) != len(cells):
+        raise ValueError("recipe cells are not the exact F0/F1 × lag1/16 × A/B/C panel")
+    expected_seeds = {0: 1001, 1: 1002}
+    if any(int(cell["seed"]) != expected_seeds[int(cell["fold"])] for cell in cells):
+        raise ValueError("recipe cell seed differs from its fold assignment")
+    if len({str(cell["run"]) for cell in cells}) != 12:
+        raise ValueError("recipe contains duplicate run identities")
+    if len({str(cell["output"]) for cell in cells}) != 12:
+        raise ValueError("recipe contains duplicate output directories")
+    if recipe.get("new_gru_fits") != 0 or recipe.get("new_teacher_fits") != 0:
+        raise ValueError("recipe includes unplanned teacher or GRU fits")
+
+    scratch = Path(recipe["resource_contract"]["scratch"]).resolve()
+    for cell in cells:
+        if not _resolve(root, cell["output"]).is_relative_to(scratch):
+            raise ValueError("candidate output directory escapes physical scratch")
+    folds = {int(fold["fold"]): fold for fold in recipe.get("folds", [])}
+    if set(folds) != {0, 1}:
+        raise ValueError("recipe must freeze exactly F0 and F1")
+    for fold_id, record in folds.items():
+        if int(record["seed"]) != expected_seeds[fold_id]:
+            raise ValueError(f"F{fold_id} recipe seed differs from its panel")
+        split_path = _resolve(root, record["split_manifest"])
+        subset_path = _resolve(root, record["subset"]["path"])
+        _require_sha(split_path, record["split_manifest_sha256"], "campaign split")
+        _require_sha(subset_path, record["subset"]["sha256"], "fit subset")
+        if not _resolve(root, record["parent_cache"]).is_relative_to(scratch):
+            raise ValueError(f"F{fold_id} parent cache escapes physical scratch")

+        raise ValueError("recipe has no pinned official target cache")

+def _canonical_json_sha256(value: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
+    raw = json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False).encode("ascii")

+
+def _expect_path_hash(

+    if value.get(hash_key) != expected_sha:

+"""Exact file and metric helpers for the online relationship screen grader."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import math
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any  # NumPy's parsed header does not expose a precise static type.
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))
+sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
+
+import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
+from grade_prediction_bank import score  # noqa: E402
+
+from wnn.evaluation import (  # noqa: E402
+    paired_component_bootstrap,
+    paired_component_moments,
+)
+
+ROWS = 20_000
+SCORED_FROM_ROW = 99
+TIME_BINS = ((99, 500), (500, 2_000), (2_000, 10_000), (10_000, ROWS))
+BOOTSTRAP_DRAWS = 2_000
+BOOTSTRAP_SEED = 271828
+
+
+def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
+    """Hash a file in bounded memory."""
+    digest = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open("rb") as stream:
+        for chunk in iter(lambda: stream.read(1 << 20), b""):
+            digest.update(chunk)
+    return digest.hexdigest()
+
+
+def npy_coverage(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Parse an NPY header and prove that its file has exactly the declared payload."""
+    with path.open("rb") as stream:
+        version = np.lib.format.read_magic(stream)
+        if version == (1, 0):
+            shape, fortran_order, dtype = np.lib.format.read_array_header_1_0(stream)
+        elif version in ((2, 0), (3, 0)):
+            shape, fortran_order, dtype = np.lib.format.read_array_header_2_0(stream)
+        else:
+            raise ValueError(f"{path}: unsupported NPY version {version}")
+        header_bytes = stream.tell()
+    if fortran_order:
+        raise ValueError(f"{path}: expected C-order NPY data")
+    dtype = np.dtype(dtype)
+    payload_bytes = math.prod(shape) * dtype.itemsize
+    file_bytes = path.stat().st_size
+    if file_bytes != header_bytes + payload_bytes:
+        raise ValueError(f"{path}: NPY file length differs from header payload coverage")
+    return {
+        "shape": list(shape),
+        "dtype": dtype.str,
+        "header_bytes": header_bytes,
+        "payload_bytes": payload_bytes,
+        "file_bytes": file_bytes,
+    }
+
+
+def prediction_memmap(
+    path: Path,
+    expected_shape: tuple[int, int, int],
+    expected_sha256: str,
+    *,
+    expected_dtype: str = "<f4",
+) -> tuple[np.ndarray, dict[str, Any]]:
+    """Verify byte coverage, fp32 shape and file hash before opening a prediction map."""
+    coverage = npy_coverage(path)
+    if coverage["shape"] != list(expected_shape) or coverage["dtype"] != expected_dtype:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{path}: expected {expected_dtype} {expected_shape}, got "
+            f"{coverage['dtype']} {tuple(coverage['shape'])}"
+        )
+    actual_sha256 = sha256_file(path)
+    if actual_sha256 != expected_sha256:
+        raise ValueError(f"{path}: prediction SHA256 differs from its frozen sidecar")
+    array = np.load(path, mmap_mode="r", allow_pickle=False)
+    if array.shape != expected_shape or array.dtype.str != expected_dtype:
+        raise ValueError(f"{path}: NPY loader disagrees with parsed header")
+    return array, {**coverage, "sha256": actual_sha256}
+
+
+def official_scores(
+    targets: np.ndarray, mask: np.ndarray, prediction: np.ndarray
+) -> dict[str, dict[str, float | int | str]]:
+    """Return official overall and fixed-bin global WP/T0/T1 scores."""
+    scored = np.asarray(mask, dtype=bool) & (np.arange(ROWS)[None, :] >= SCORED_FROM_ROW)
+    result = {"overall": score(targets, scored, prediction)}
+    for start, stop in TIME_BINS:
+        bin_mask = scored.copy()
+        bin_mask[:, :start] = False
+        bin_mask[:, stop:] = False
+        result[f"rows_{start}_{stop}"] = score(targets, bin_mask, prediction)
+    return result
+
+
+def paired_endpoint_moments(
+    targets: np.ndarray, prediction: np.ndarray, scored_mask: np.ndarray
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Compute canonical centered per-sequence moments for one fixed endpoint."""
+    candidate, _ = paired_component_moments(targets, prediction, prediction, scored_mask)
+    return candidate
+
+
+def paired_component_contrast(
+    targets: np.ndarray,
+    mask: np.ndarray,
+    candidate: np.ndarray,
+    reference: np.ndarray,
+    components: np.ndarray,
+    candidate_scores: dict[str, dict[str, float | int | str]],
+    reference_scores: dict[str, dict[str, float | int | str]],
+    candidate_moments: np.ndarray | None = None,
+    reference_moments: np.ndarray | None = None,
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Report fixed-model target/bin deltas and an overall official-WP component interval."""
+    if candidate_moments is None or reference_moments is None:
+        candidate_moments, reference_moments = paired_component_moments(
+            targets, candidate, reference, mask
+        )
+    interval = paired_component_bootstrap(
+        candidate_moments,
+        reference_moments,
+        components,
+        n_boot=BOOTSTRAP_DRAWS,
+        seed=BOOTSTRAP_SEED,
+        centered=True,
+    )
+    deltas: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {}
+    for band, candidate_result in candidate_scores.items():
+        reference_result = reference_scores[band]
+        deltas[band] = {
+            metric: float(candidate_result[metric] - reference_result[metric])
+            for metric in ("wp", "t0", "t1")
+        }
+    return {
+        "point_deltas": deltas,
+        "overall_official_wp_paired_component_bootstrap": interval,
+        "uncertainty_scope": "conditional on these fixed fitted endpoints; no training-seed variance",
+    }

+"""Checks for row weights, inherited normalization and fixed training records."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+from typing import Any  # JSON metadata is validated at runtime.
+
+import numpy as np
+from online_relationship_grade_contract import ROW_WEIGHT_CONTRACT, ROWS
+
+
+def verify_row_weight_contract(run: str, value: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """Bind candidate provenance to the shared canonical FP32 propensity weights."""
+    if value.get("args") != ROW_WEIGHT_CONTRACT:
+        raise ValueError(f"{run}: fit row-weight arguments differ from the recipe")
+    if value.get("batch_semantics") != (
+        "one complete sequence per main_row_weights call; true-mask mass scale is sequence-local"
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(f"{run}: fitting normalization is not sequence-local")
+
+
+def verify_parent_normalization(fold: dict[str, Any], normalization: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """Check the readout inherits the exact selected parent's mean and standard deviation."""
+    parent = fold["parent"]
+    for field, identity in (("parent_mean", "mean_identity"), ("parent_std", "std_identity")):
+        value = np.asarray(normalization.get(field), dtype="<f4")
+        if value.shape != (211,) or not np.isfinite(value).all():
+            raise ValueError(f"F{fold['fold']} candidate {field} is malformed")
+        if hashlib.sha256(value.tobytes()).hexdigest() != parent[identity]:
+            raise ValueError(f"F{fold['fold']} candidate {field} differs from the frozen parent")
+        if field == "parent_std" and np.any(value <= 0):
+            raise ValueError(f"F{fold['fold']} candidate parent std is not positive")
+
+
+def verify_fit_records(
+    run: str,
+    recipe: dict[str, Any],
+    cell: dict[str, Any],
+    fit_refs: list[dict[str, Any]],
+    fit: dict[str, Any],
+    normalizer: dict[str, Any],
+    normalization: dict[str, Any],
+) -> None:
+    """Require the exact three-epoch, fixed-order full-membership optimization receipt."""
+    records = fit.get("epoch_records")
+    expected_rows = len(fit_refs) * ROWS
+    expected_updates = (expected_rows + int(recipe["readout"]["batch_rows"]) - 1) // int(
+        recipe["readout"]["batch_rows"]
+    )
+    if not isinstance(records, list) or len(records) != 3:
+        raise ValueError(f"{run}: provenance must contain three epoch records")
+    for epoch_index, record in enumerate(records):
+        if (
+            record.get("epoch") != epoch_index
+            or record.get("updates") != expected_updates
+            or record.get("finite_updates") != expected_updates
+            or record.get("fit_sequences") != len(fit_refs)
+            or record.get("fit_rows") != expected_rows
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(f"{run}: epoch {epoch_index} lacks the complete fixed update budget")
+        for metric in (
+            "mean_batch_primary_pair_wmse",
+            "mean_preclip_gradient_norm",
+            "max_preclip_gradient_norm",
+        ):
+            if not np.isfinite(float(record.get(metric, np.nan))):
+                raise ValueError(f"{run}: epoch {epoch_index} has a nonfinite {metric}")
+    metadata = fit.get("metadata", {})
+    expected_hparams = {
+        "arm": str(cell["arm"]),
+        "lag": int(cell["lag"]),
+        "seed": int(cell["seed"]),
+        "epochs": 3,
+        "fixed_checkpoint_epoch": 2,
+        "batch_rows": int(recipe["readout"]["batch_rows"]),
+        "learning_rate": float(recipe["readout"]["lr"]),
+        "weight_decay": float(recipe["readout"]["weight_decay"]),
+        "gradient_clip": float(recipe["readout"]["clip"]),
+    }
+    if any(metadata.get(key) != value for key, value in expected_hparams.items()):
+        raise ValueError(f"{run}: fitter metadata differs from the frozen head recipe")
+    if metadata.get("relationship_normalizer") != normalizer:
+        raise ValueError(f"{run}: fitter metadata has a different relationship normalizer")
+    if metadata.get("parent_mean") != normalization.get("parent_mean") or metadata.get(
+        "parent_std"
+    ) != normalization.get("parent_std"):
+        raise ValueError(f"{run}: fitter metadata does not inherit the frozen parent normalization")

+"""Score fixed endpoints and paired fold-local contrasts using canonical metrics."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any  # Report records have runtime-defined score and interval fields.
+
+import numpy as np
+from online_relationship_grade_contract import ARMS, CandidateArtifacts, ParentCacheArtifacts
+from online_relationship_grade_core import (
+    ROWS,
+    official_scores,
+    paired_component_contrast,
+    paired_endpoint_moments,
+)
+
+PRIMARY_PAIRS = (("C", "A"), ("C", "B"))
+
+
+def grade_fold(
+    fold_id: int,
+    parent: ParentCacheArtifacts,
+    candidates: dict[tuple[int, int, str], CandidateArtifacts],
+    targets: np.ndarray,
+    mask: np.ndarray,
+    components: np.ndarray,
+) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], list[dict[str, Any]]]:
+    """Score seven fixed endpoints and form thirteen fold-local paired contrasts."""
+    scored_mask = mask & (np.arange(ROWS)[None, :] >= 99)
+    endpoints: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {"parent": parent.prediction}
+    endpoint_identity = {"parent": parent.identity}
+    for lag in (1, 16):
+        for arm in ARMS:
+            name = f"{arm}_lag{lag}"
+            artifact = candidates[(fold_id, lag, arm)]
+            endpoints[name] = artifact.prediction
+            endpoint_identity[name] = artifact.identity
+
+    endpoint_scores = {
+        name: official_scores(targets, mask, prediction) for name, prediction in endpoints.items()
+    }
+    moments = {
+        name: paired_endpoint_moments(targets, prediction, scored_mask)
+        for name, prediction in endpoints.items()
+    }
+    contrasts: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+
+    def add_contrast(name: str, candidate: str, reference: str) -> None:
+        contrasts.append(
+            {
+                "contrast": name,
+                **paired_component_contrast(
+                    targets,
+                    mask,
+                    endpoints[candidate],
+                    endpoints[reference],
+                    components,
+                    endpoint_scores[candidate],
+                    endpoint_scores[reference],
+                    moments[candidate],
+                    moments[reference],
+                ),
+            }
+        )
+
+    for lag in (1, 16):
+        for candidate_arm, reference_arm in PRIMARY_PAIRS:
+            add_contrast(
+                f"{candidate_arm}-{reference_arm}_lag{lag}",
+                f"{candidate_arm}_lag{lag}",
+                f"{reference_arm}_lag{lag}",
+            )
+        for arm in ARMS:
+            add_contrast(f"{arm}-parent_lag{lag}", f"{arm}_lag{lag}", "parent")
+    for arm in ARMS:
+        add_contrast(f"lag16-lag1_{arm}", f"{arm}_lag16", f"{arm}_lag1")
+    if len(contrasts) != 13:
+        raise AssertionError("fold contrast construction did not produce thirteen pairs")
+    return (
+        {
+            "fold": fold_id,
+            "evaluation_sequences": len(targets),
+            "evaluation_components": int(len(np.unique(components))),
+            "parent": endpoint_identity["parent"],
+            "endpoints": {
+                name: {"identity": endpoint_identity[name], "scores": endpoint_scores[name]}
+                for name in endpoints
+            },
+        },
+        contrasts,
+    )

+"""Load and align outer-fold labels only after every endpoint passes validation."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any  # JSON metadata is validated at runtime.
+
+import numpy as np
+from online_relationship_grade_contract import ROWS, _require_sha, _resolve, read_json
+from online_relationship_grade_core import sha256_file
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+
+
+def load_targets(
+    recipe: dict[str, Any], fold_records: dict[int, dict[str, Any]]
+) -> tuple[np.ndarray, dict[int, tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]]]:
+    """Open outer-fold labels only after every endpoint has passed its artifact gate."""
+    target_record = recipe["target_cache"]
+    target_path = _resolve(ROOT, target_record["path"])
+    _require_sha(target_path, target_record["sha256"], "official target cache")
+    stat = target_path.stat()
+    for fold_id, fold in fold_records.items():
+        split = read_json(_resolve(ROOT, fold["split_manifest"]))
+        source = split["sources"].get("cache/valid_targets.npz", {})
+        if source.get("bytes") != stat.st_size or source.get("mtime_ns") != stat.st_mtime_ns:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"F{fold_id} target cache file identity differs from the split manifest"
+            )
+
+    with np.load(target_path, allow_pickle=False) as archive:
+        required = {"row_group", "y", "mask"}
+        if not required.issubset(archive.files):
+            raise ValueError("official target archive lacks row_group, y or mask")
+        groups = np.asarray(archive["row_group"])
+        targets = np.asarray(archive["y"])
+        mask = np.asarray(archive["mask"])
+    if groups.ndim != 1 or groups.dtype.kind not in "iu" or len(np.unique(groups)) != len(groups):
+        raise ValueError("official target row groups are malformed or duplicated")
+    if targets.shape != (len(groups), ROWS, 2) or mask.shape != (len(groups), ROWS):
+        raise ValueError("official target arrays do not match the full valid-cache schema")
+    if targets.dtype.str != "<f4":
+        raise ValueError("official target labels must use the cache's little-endian FP32 values")
+    if mask.dtype != np.bool_:
+        raise ValueError("official target score mask must be boolean")
+    if not np.isfinite(targets[mask]).all():
+        raise ValueError("official target cache contains nonfinite scored labels")
+    position = {int(group): index for index, group in enumerate(groups)}
+    folds: dict[int, tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]] = {}
+    for fold_id, fold in fold_records.items():
+        eval_groups = [int(group) for group in fold["evaluation_groups"]]
+        if any(group not in position for group in eval_groups):
+            raise ValueError(f"F{fold_id} evaluation groups are missing from the target cache")
+        indices = np.asarray([position[group] for group in eval_groups], dtype=np.int64)
+        split = read_json(_resolve(ROOT, fold["split_manifest"]))
+        component_by_group = {
+            int(record["row_group"]): int(record["component"])
+            for record in split["sequences"]["valid"]
+        }
+        components = np.asarray(
+            [component_by_group[group] for group in eval_groups], dtype=np.int64
+        )
+        folds[fold_id] = targets[indices], mask[indices], components
+    if sha256_file(target_path) != target_record["sha256"]:
+        raise ValueError("official target cache changed during scoring")
+    return groups, folds

+"""Small synthetic checks for immutable grader gates and canonical scoring."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import numpy as np
+from online_relationship_grade_contract import row_refs_sha256, validate_recipe
+from online_relationship_grade_core import (
+    npy_coverage,
+    official_scores,
+    paired_component_contrast,
+    paired_endpoint_moments,
+    prediction_memmap,
+    sha256_file,
+)
+from online_relationship_grade_parent import verify_parent_prediction_metadata
+
+
+class GraderContractTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_runner_execution_status_is_accepted_without_target_access(self) -> None:
+        root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+        template_path = (
+            root / "research/experiment_drafts/online-relationships-20261022/recipe.json"
+        )
+        recipe = json.loads(template_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+        recipe["status"] = "admitted_for_execution"
+        recipe["admitted_new_fits"] = 12
+        recipe["target_cache"]["path"] = str(root / "missing-target-cache-not-opened.npz")
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
+            recipe_path = Path(directory) / "execution-recipe.json"
+            recipe_path.write_text(json.dumps(recipe), encoding="utf-8")
+            loaded, _ = validate_recipe(recipe_path, root, sha256_file(recipe_path))
+        self.assertEqual(loaded["status"], "admitted_for_execution")
+
+    def test_npy_header_must_cover_exact_payload(self) -> None:
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
+            path = Path(directory) / "pred.npy"
+            np.save(path, np.zeros((2, 20000, 2), dtype="<f4"), allow_pickle=False)
+            coverage = npy_coverage(path)
+            self.assertEqual(coverage["shape"], [2, 20000, 2])
+            prediction, _ = prediction_memmap(path, (2, 20000, 2), sha256_file(path))
+            self.assertEqual(prediction.dtype.str, "<f4")
+            with path.open("ab") as stream:
+                stream.write(b"x")
+            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "file length"):
+                npy_coverage(path)
+
+    def test_source_qualified_membership_digest_is_ordered(self) -> None:
+        first = [
+            {"split": "train", "row_group": 3},
+            {"split": "valid", "row_group": 7},
+        ]
+        self.assertEqual(row_refs_sha256(first), row_refs_sha256(first.copy()))
+        self.assertNotEqual(row_refs_sha256(first), row_refs_sha256(list(reversed(first))))
+        changed = [dict(first[0]), {"split": "train", "row_group": 7}]
+        self.assertNotEqual(row_refs_sha256(first), row_refs_sha256(changed))
+
+    def test_deferred_recipe_is_rejected_before_artifact_or_target_access(self) -> None:
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
+            root = Path(directory)
+            recipe_path = root / "recipe.json"
+            recipe_path.write_text(
+                json.dumps(
+                    {
+                        "schema": "wnn.online-relationships.v1",
+                        "experiment_id": "E-ONLINE-RELATIONSHIPS-20261022-R1",
+                        "status": "deferred_entire_panel_after_feature_cost_profile",
+                    }
+                ),
+                encoding="utf-8",
+            )
+            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "not root-admitted"):
+                validate_recipe(recipe_path, root, sha256_file(recipe_path))
+
+    def test_parent_sidecar_matches_delivery_schema_and_parent_identity(self) -> None:
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
+            root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+            scratch = Path(directory)
+            recipe_path = (
+                root / "research/experiment_drafts/online-relationships-20261022/recipe.json"
+            )
+            eval_meta_path = scratch / "evaluation_sequences.json"
+            eval_meta_path.write_text("{}\n", encoding="utf-8")
+            prediction_path = scratch / "evaluation_predictions.npy"
+            prediction_meta_path = scratch / "evaluation_predictions.json"
+            recipe = {"recipe_id": "test-recipe"}
+            parent = {"run": "frozen-parent", "epoch": 5}
+            fold = {
+                "fold": 0,
+                "seed": 1001,
+                "parent": parent,
+                "split_manifest_sha256": "split-sha",
+            }
+            refs = [{"split": "valid", "row_group": 7}]
+            eval_meta = {
+                "parent": {"endpoint_precision": "strict_fp32", "endpoint_backend": "cpu"},
+                "parent_prediction_file": prediction_path.name,
+                "parent_prediction_sha256": "prediction-sha",
+            }
+            metadata = {
+                "schema": "wnn.online-relationships.parent-predictions.v1",
+                "scope": "feature_only_eval",
+                "recipe_id": recipe["recipe_id"],
+                "recipe": str(recipe_path.resolve()),
+                "recipe_sha256": "recipe-sha",
+                "fold": 0,
+                "seed": 1001,
+                "parent": parent,
+                "split_manifest_sha256": fold["split_manifest_sha256"],
+                "evaluation_cache_sidecar": str(eval_meta_path),
+                "evaluation_cache_sidecar_sha256": sha256_file(eval_meta_path),
+                "row_refs": refs,
+                "membership_sha256": row_refs_sha256(refs),
+                "prediction_file": prediction_path.name,
+                "prediction_path": str(prediction_path),
+                "prediction_sha256": "prediction-sha",
+                "shape": [1, 20000, 2],
+                "dtype": "<f4",
+                "endpoint": {"precision": "strict_fp32", "backend": "cpu"},
+                "sampled_profile": False,
+            }
+            observed = verify_parent_prediction_metadata(
+                root,
+                recipe,
+                "recipe-sha",
+                fold,
+                recipe_path,
+                refs,
+                eval_meta_path,
+                eval_meta,
+                prediction_path,
+                prediction_meta_path,
+                metadata,
+            )
+            self.assertEqual(observed, "prediction-sha")
+            metadata["parent"] = eval_meta["parent"]
+            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "metadata is inconsistent"):
+                verify_parent_prediction_metadata(
+                    root,
+                    recipe,
+                    "recipe-sha",
+                    fold,
+                    recipe_path,
+                    refs,
+                    eval_meta_path,
+                    eval_meta,
+                    prediction_path,
+                    prediction_meta_path,
+                    metadata,
+                )
+
+    def test_official_scores_and_component_contrast_use_fixed_bins(self) -> None:
+        rows = np.arange(20000, dtype=np.float32)
+        target = np.stack((np.sin(rows / 11), np.cos(rows / 17)), axis=-1)[None]
+        mask = np.ones((1, 20000), dtype=bool)
+        candidate = (target + np.float32(0.03)).astype(np.float32)
+        reference = (target - np.float32(0.04)).astype(np.float32)
+        candidate_scores = official_scores(target, mask, candidate)
+        reference_scores = official_scores(target, mask, reference)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            set(candidate_scores),
+            {"overall", "rows_99_500", "rows_500_2000", "rows_2000_10000", "rows_10000_20000"},
+        )
+        selected = mask & (rows[None, :] >= 99)
+        candidate_moments = paired_endpoint_moments(target, candidate, selected)
+        reference_moments = paired_endpoint_moments(target, reference, selected)
+        result = paired_component_contrast(
+            target,
+            mask,
+            candidate,
+            reference,
+            np.asarray([42]),
+            candidate_scores,
+            reference_scores,
+            candidate_moments,
+            reference_moments,
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(
+            result["overall_official_wp_paired_component_bootstrap"]["n_components"], 1
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(set(result["point_deltas"]), set(candidate_scores))
+        self.assertEqual(set(result["point_deltas"]["overall"]), {"wp", "t0", "t1"})
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

The 52 index correspondences are a tested representation assumption, not known economic relationships. All state depends only on observed inputs, never targets, scoring masks or request flags. +# Independent critique of the fresh input-representation cards
+
+## Verdict and scope
+
+The four directions remain plausible proposals, with three distinct new mechanisms: shared pair pooling (H-395), input-triggered update skipping (H-396), and a randomized degree-two sidecar (H-397). Per-channel age is an elaboration of the already retained H-PER-FIELD-AGE-20261022-R1, not a new arm. The cited papers support the component methods in their original settings; none establishes Challenge2 quality or runtime improvement.
+
+This is a source-only review of the [cards](../ideas/FRESH_REFRAME_20261023_R1.md), [source receipt](../sources/FRESH_REFRAME_SOURCES_20261023_R1.md), [reframe contract](../../campaign_2026-10-21/next_cycle_r1/REFRAME_CONTRACT_R1.json), objective, tree mappings, and cited primary papers. I did not inspect model code, data, predictions or run receipts; perform a data scan, replay, fit, test or profile; or assign numerical priors. All local folds are exposed. No test is admitted by this review. The contract grants zero additional fits to reframing, and the in-flight 12-head panel should proceed independently.
+
+The proposal notes disclose that a broad search exposed fragments of older idea notes before the cards were committed. That weakens the claim of blind first-proposal independence; retain the cards as source-grounded proposals and keep the exposure attached to later interpretation. This critique is an independent review of the written sources, not a blind ideation replication.
+
+## Cheapest discriminating tests
+
+Counts below assume two predeclared source-qualified fold/seed cells and no exact same-stage controls already available. A control is reusable only if its parent checkpoint, training stage, optimizer state where relevant, membership, sampling, normalization, update budget and selection rule match. Freeze the exact cell IDs, parent hashes, feature/metric implementation, and primary comparison before any outcomes are read. All fits listed are student fits; teacher fits are zero.
+
+| Rank by immediate cost | Direction | Minimal comparison and count | What it can establish |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| 1 | H-396 update skip | **0 optimizer fits**; replay one frozen parent on one admitted exposed fold through two inference paths: ordinary update at every row (control) and one predeclared nonzero threshold (candidate). One checkpoint, two prediction paths; timing repeats do not add fits. | Whether this fixed inference rule trades official endpoint quality for measured runtime on that checkpoint and fold. It does not test a learned Skip RNN gate or train-time quality. |
+| 2 (tie) | Existing per-channel age | **4 new fits**: age sidecar and same-shape zero-age/raw control, each on both cells. | Whether age inputs help beyond the matched parent adaptation. This is a follow-up to the existing hypothesis, not a new ID. |
+| 2 (tie) | H-397 TensorSketch | **4 new fits**: raw-plus-one frozen sketch and same-shape zero-sketch control, each on both cells. Freeze one dimension and one map seed first. | Whether this fixed sketch helps in this student recipe. A second hash or the other dimension is a later configuration and needs its own selection accounting. |
+| 4 | H-395 pair encoder | **6 new fits**: raw-only, proposed pairing, and one fixed deranged pairing, each on both cells. | Whether the proposed correspondence beats both the unchanged input recipe and a same-capacity pairing control. |
+
+Exact controls can reduce new fits only when they already match the stated stage and cell. No such reusable same-stage controls were identified in this source review, so 6/4/4 is the defensible planning count for the proposed two-cell student screens. Do not compare a newly fine-tuned challenger to an unadapted parent and attribute the delta to its feature sidecar. These alternatives are separate arms: the 4–6 total-fit screen policy does not authorize running all of them together, and none has current fit authority. H-396's lower fit count also does not grant replay authority; its card correctly requires separate root admission for any data read.
+
+For H-396, a fixed threshold ladder would add configurations and selection exposure. The first screen should use a single threshold selected by a frozen training-input-only rule, with the zero-threshold path as control. Report the complete official metric as the primary outcome, plus skipped-row share, scored-row and official label-weight coverage within skip regions, per-target weighted contributions by quiet-run length/position, and end-to-end runtime. The bucket views diagnose why a result changed; they cannot replace the full endpoint because a skipped state update can affect later predictions. Define the quality/runtime comparison rule before replay instead of leaving “near the parent” or “useful runtime savings” subjective.
+
+## Mechanism and control findings
+
+**H-395 — conditional pass after count correction.** [Deep Sets](https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.06114) studies functions invariant to permutations of set elements. That result applies only if the proposed pair elements have a useful exchangeability symmetry. Anonymous column names and the hypothesized 52 `i1`/`i0` correspondences do not establish such symmetry. The raw bypass is a good protection for fixed channel identity; keep the pair map and its direction convention frozen. The deranged control must preserve the same architecture, pair count, feature scaling and initialization, changing only the correspondence map. A raw-only control is also needed to tell whether the sidecar helps at all.
+
+The card's “four fits” and “two challenger fits” alternatives do not say which arms those counts include, while the intervention and falsifier name raw-only, proposed-map, and deranged-map endpoints. The full matched comparison is three arms × two cells = six fits when none of those endpoints is an exact reusable match; the current tree entry records this design. A valid four-fit shortcut is to fit only the proposed and deranged maps on both cells and report the frozen raw parent as an **unadapted reference**. That tests map-specific value but leaves the candidate-versus-parent delta confounded by additional adaptation. Two new fits would require exact same-stage raw and deranged controls for both cells, leaving only the proposed map to fit; no such artifacts were identified here. State which design is intended and align the card text to it.
+
+**Per-channel age — source-grounded elaboration, with an operational definition still missing.** [GRU-D](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.01865) uses masks and elapsed time for irregular or missing clinical observations. Challenge2 rows are observed, so informative missingness does not transfer. A narrower transferable component is per-feature elapsed time since a causal, train-calibrated change event. Define the change tolerance and age cap per feature from fitting inputs only, append age beside the raw path, and reset ages at every sequence boundary. Without a fixed tolerance, ages may mostly encode floating-point jitter or become nearly constant. Keep the existing H-PER-FIELD-AGE ID and provenance; the new card is not duplicate scientific evidence.
+
+For the 4-fit comparison, keep the parent function identical at initialization: zero-initialize the new sidecar's contribution, then fit age and zero-age controls with the same parent, stages and update budget. This makes the treatment the information in age rather than a changed cold-start function or extra input-head capacity. The card's proposed falsifier “nearly every feature resets every row” requires a fitting-only input diagnostic; that diagnostic is useful but was not run or authorized here.
+
+**H-396 — good cheap falsifier, but a different claim from the cited method.** [Skip RNN](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.06834) learns when to skip updates and uses update-budget pressure. A standardized input-difference threshold is a deterministic heuristic, not a reproduction of that learned gate. It assumes low input novelty means the recurrent state is not useful to update; long unchanged-input runs can still contain target changes or accumulated state error. The frozen-checkpoint replay is a defensible first test of inference-time quality/runtime only. Freeze the training-only scaling, threshold tie rule, first-row forced update and gate computation. Read out every required row, hold state only on skipped steps, and reset previous-input and recurrent state at sequence boundaries. If gating overhead erases the recurrent savings or later outputs degrade, the stated inference claim fails on this screen; one fold remains a cheap exposed-data screen, not a family-wide rejection.
+
+**H-397 — conditional pass, with a narrow approximation claim.** Pham and Pagh's [TensorSketch paper](https://researcher.itu.dk/en/publications/fast-and-scalable-polynomial-kernels-via-explicit-feature-maps/) uses CountSketch and convolution to approximate polynomial-kernel features. That establishes a way to construct a randomized interaction map, not that appending it to a nonlinear recurrent model improves this endpoint. The paper's asymptotic cost is not a local training or serving guarantee. Fix either 32 or 64 dimensions and the exact hash/sign maps before the first screen; test one hash across the two paired cells, then treat another hash as a new follow-up. Otherwise a dimension/hash sweep silently expands selection. Use a matched zero-sketch sidecar so both arms have the same model shape and parent function at initialization. Record collisions/map hashes and check training/export operator parity under strict FP32; confirm the chosen FFT/convolution implementation is deterministic on the serving path. Profile full per-row and full-sequence costs before fit admission, since the input is dense and there are about 20,000 rows.
+
+## Shared invariants and one transferable component
+
+Every eventual comparison must preserve strict FP32 with autocast and TF32 off, deterministic feature maps/gates, causal prefix-only computation, sequence-state reset, source-qualified memberships, and the fixed `global_wp_clip2_v1` outcome: fixed `need_prediction AND is_scored` mask, clipping at ±2, original clipped-label magnitude weights, and the mean over both targets. Fit all normalization, thresholds and tolerances using fitting inputs only; do not use validation labels to define events. Compare complete endpoints against matched controls. Report the two-cell paired deltas and model-seed/fold exposure separately; conditional component resampling on these exposed folds does not provide fresh confirmation or public-transfer evidence.
+
+One defensible transfer is GRU-D's per-channel elapsed-time state, limited to **time since last meaningful input change**. Keep raw values, add a causal age with fit-only threshold/scale, and reset it per sequence. Do not import the missingness-mask or clinical missingness claim. This supplies a concrete, low-dimensional feature to test while preserving the parent path.
+
+## Provenance and review status
+
+The assigned request route was native Codex (GPT-6-based); this subagent did not receive an exact model-version or reasoning-effort field, so the repository's Luna/max role preference cannot be verified as the executed variant. No external model, CLI provider or teammate was consulted. Primary-source checks were the linked arXiv abstracts for Deep Sets, GRU-D and Skip RNN and the IT University of Copenhagen publication page for TensorSketch; these confirm the source component summaries and scope limits above. No source paper reports a Challenge2 result.
+
+Review decision: **retain the four directions as proposals; correct H-395's fit-count text; keep per-channel age on its existing ID; freeze one H-397 dimension/hash; require a concrete threshold and quality/runtime rule for H-396. No fit, replay, scan, test, profile, score, numerical prior, or public forecast is authorized or claimed by this review.**

+# Strict-FP32 Numba online relationship stream code/math review R1
+
+This is an independent source and recurrence review of the optional compiled
+online relationship transform. I found no semantic difference from the Python
+reference by inspection. This review does not establish runtime speed or a
+training result.
+
+## Source and scope
+
+- Reviewed actor commit: `46b7ff106875acc30259a3be1abb33f3313d90ee`.
+- The same compiled implementation is present at root integration commit
+  `c0c1c639bca2babbf03981e42f878619817ab6a0`.
+- The Python reference in `src/wnn/online_relationship.py` is unchanged by the
+  actor commit except for the new `transform_compiled` adapter. Its parent blob
+  is `e2cc59cb58c89f05442dcec46ee7d7024c961106`.
+- Reviewed the [Numba kernel](../../../src/wnn/online_relationship_numba.py),
+  [adapter and Python transform](../../../src/wnn/online_relationship.py), and
+  [scalar-oracle and chunk-continuation tests](../../../tests/test_online_relationship_numba.py).
+  No tests or benchmarks were run during this independent review because the
+  root agent reserved the CPU slot.
+
+## Recurrence check
+
+The kernel is decorated with `njit(cache=True, fastmath=False, parallel=False)`
+and loops over rows and channels serially. Its online state and output arrays
+are FP32. Arithmetic that feeds the recurrence has explicit FP32 conversions;
+the update equations follow the Python path's operation order.
+
+At row `t`, the kernel forms `u[t] = i1[t] - i1[t-lag]` when available and
+stores that standardized, clipped value in the 16-row ring. The matured target
+at `t >= 16` is `v[t] = i0[t] - i0[t-16]`, paired with the stored `u[t-16]`.
+Unavailable `u` values are zero. For lag 16, this means matured rows 16 through
+31 have the specified zero regressor; row 32 is the first matured pair with a
+real regressor.
+
+The error uses the coefficient state before the current pair update. The
+forecast and emitted slope use the state after the update and the current
+`u[t]`. Arm A keeps slope zero while maintaining the shared mean/statistic
+state; arm B updates on matured rows 16 through 98 inclusive and freezes at row
+99; arm C continues updating. The ring slots, reset count, and state mutation
+also match the Python implementation for chunked calls. Each emitted component
+is clipped to ±8, as are the standardized differences.
+
+The new tests compare every output and final state array against a scalar FP32
+oracle for all six arm/lag combinations. They also cover chunk restore and
+mixing compiled and Python chunks. Root reports that the bounded test run
+passed 35 tests bitwise with peak RSS 229,548 KiB; I did not independently

+# Sources for the online relationship amendment
+
+These sources motivate components of [H-ONLINE-RELATIONSHIPS](../ideas/ONLINE_RELATIONSHIPS_20261022_R1.md), [per-field age](../ideas/PER_FIELD_AGE_20261022_R1.md), and [burstiness](../ideas/BURSTINESS_20261022_R1.md). They establish no Challenge2 gain.
+
+- Sun et al., [Test-Time Training with Self-Supervision for Generalization under Distribution Shifts](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.13231), ICML2020. The inspected primary abstract describes self-supervised updates using unlabeled test samples and an online extension, evaluated on image classification. The local proposal instead fits a fixed task readout over an adapting scalar input model; it is not a replication of that method.
+- Che et al., [Recurrent Neural Networks for Multivariate Time Series with Missing Values](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.01865),2016. The primary abstract describes masks and time intervals in GRU-D for informative missingness. Timing motivates the separate age representation; unchanged fields here are not known missing observations.
+- Barndorff-Nielsen and Shephard, [Power and Bipower Variation with Stochastic Volatility and Jumps](https://shephard.scholars.harvard.edu/publications/power-and-bipower-variation-stochastic-volatility-and-jumps),2004. The author's publication record and [Oxford archive](https://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid%3Af927c62c-1717-4a27-8518-d272b0459d85) support the source identity. The originally supplied Nuffield PDF URL was inaccessible to the browser; no claim of reading that full PDF. Transfer is only the descriptive adjacent-product component, not the asymptotic jump interpretation.
+

+
+[Exact selection receipt](../../experiment_drafts/online-relationships-20261022/RANDOM_SOURCE_R1.json): seed20261022; sort non-README .txt/.md files in competition-writeups, split blank-line paragraphs, keep non-heading paragraphs of at least200characters, and choose uniformly with Python random.Random. There were86 candidates. The draw selected paragraph22 of the [Santander translated transcript](competition-writeups/santander_transcript_english_translation.md), SHA2568451ef219a1ee6b20f5e192b581e2f511f3f9a26d61f0f20f823da651765509b.
+
+The selected passage reports unsuccessful attempts to infer latent representations, categories, and time structure in anonymous columns. The transferable caution is to measure task utility rather than assume an economic relationship from column correspondence. An unconventional alternative would learn a sparse correspondence rather than fix indices, but it would introduce selection and fitting costs and is **not admitted**. This external static-data failure does not refute the causal stream hypothesis. The exact passage is preserved in the receipt rather than reconstructed from memory.

+"""Causal online i1-to-i0 relationship features for matched residual screens."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import math
+from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Literal, cast
+
+import numpy as np
+
+from wnn.data import FEATURE_COLUMNS, I0, I1, N_FEATURES
+from wnn.features import N_EVENT_FEATURES
+
+OnlineRelationshipArm = Literal["A", "B", "C"]
+OnlineRelationshipLag = Literal[1, 16]
+HORIZON = 16
+CHANNELS = 52
+FEATURE_WIDTH = 4 * CHANNELS
+BASE_INPUT_WIDTH = N_FEATURES + N_EVENT_FEATURES
+MODEL_INPUT_WIDTH = BASE_INPUT_WIDTH + FEATURE_WIDTH
+FEATURE_NAMES = (
+    tuple(f"matured_{name}" for name in FEATURE_COLUMNS[:CHANNELS])
+    + tuple(f"forecast_{name}" for name in FEATURE_COLUMNS[:CHANNELS])
+    + tuple(f"error_{name}" for name in FEATURE_COLUMNS[:CHANNELS])
+    + tuple(f"slope_{name}" for name in FEATURE_COLUMNS[:CHANNELS])
+)
+NORMALIZER_FLOOR = np.float32(0.001)
+FEATURE_CLIP = np.float32(8.0)
+_DECAY = np.float32(math.exp2(-1.0 / 512.0))
+_UPDATE = np.float32(1.0 - float(_DECAY))
+_VARIANCE_EPSILON = np.float32(0.1)
+_SCHEMA = "online_i1_i0_relationship_v3"
+_I0_CHANNELS = slice(I0.bid_px.start, I0.trade_vol.stop)
+_I1_CHANNELS = slice(I1.bid_px.start, I1.trade_vol.stop)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class OnlineRelationshipNormalizer:
+    """Fitting-only standardization for the 52-channel u and v differences."""
+
+    u_mean: np.ndarray
+    u_scale: np.ndarray
+    v_mean: np.ndarray
+    v_scale: np.ndarray
+    lag: OnlineRelationshipLag
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        """Validate and freeze separate fitting statistics for both differences."""
+        _validate_lag(self.lag)
+        for name in ("u_mean", "u_scale", "v_mean", "v_scale"):
+            value = np.asarray(getattr(self, name), dtype=np.float32)
+            if value.shape != (CHANNELS,) or not np.isfinite(value).all():
+                raise ValueError("relationship normalization requires 52 finite values per vector")
+            if name.endswith("scale") and np.any(value < NORMALIZER_FLOOR):
+                raise ValueError("relationship normalization scales must be at least 0.001")
+            value = value.copy()
+            value.flags.writeable = False
+            object.__setattr__(self, name, value)
+
+    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:
+        """Return the stable JSON-compatible normalizer representation."""
+        return {
+            "schema": _SCHEMA,
+            "lag": self.lag,
+            "u_mean": self.u_mean.tolist(),
+            "u_scale": self.u_scale.tolist(),
+            "v_mean": self.v_mean.tolist(),
+            "v_scale": self.v_scale.tolist(),
+        }
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_dict(cls, value: Mapping[str, object]) -> OnlineRelationshipNormalizer:
+        """Validate and restore a fitting-only normalizer representation."""
+        if value.get("schema") != _SCHEMA:
+            raise ValueError("relationship normalizer has an unsupported schema")
+        return cls(
+            np.asarray(value.get("u_mean"), dtype=np.float32),
+            np.asarray(value.get("u_scale"), dtype=np.float32),
+            np.asarray(value.get("v_mean"), dtype=np.float32),
+            np.asarray(value.get("v_scale"), dtype=np.float32),
+            cast(OnlineRelationshipLag, value.get("lag")),
+        )
+
+
+def fit_online_relationship_normalizer(
+    raw_sequences: Iterable[np.ndarray], lag: OnlineRelationshipLag
+) -> OnlineRelationshipNormalizer:
+    """Fit separate u/v means and scales from the supplied fitting sequences only.
+
+    The caller owns and records source-qualified membership. u statistics use
+    rows where the selected i1 lag exists; v statistics use rows from maturity
+    row 16. The downstream regression still consumes zero-u placeholders for
+    earlier matured pairs (16 of its 83 B updates when lag is 16).
+    """
+    _validate_lag(lag)
+    u_mean = np.zeros(CHANNELS, dtype=np.float32)
+    u_m2 = np.zeros(CHANNELS, dtype=np.float32)
+    v_mean = np.zeros(CHANNELS, dtype=np.float32)
+    v_m2 = np.zeros(CHANNELS, dtype=np.float32)
+    u_count = 0
+    v_count = 0
+    sequence_count = 0
+    for raw in raw_sequences:
+        sequence = _validate_sequence(raw)
+        if not len(sequence):
+            continue
+        sequence_count += 1
+        if len(sequence) > lag:
+            u = sequence[lag:, _I1_CHANNELS] - sequence[:-lag, _I1_CHANNELS]
+            u_mean, u_m2 = _merge_centered_moments(u_mean, u_m2, u_count, u)
+            u_count += len(u)
+        if len(sequence) > HORIZON:
+            v = sequence[HORIZON:, _I0_CHANNELS] - sequence[:-HORIZON, _I0_CHANNELS]
+            v_mean, v_m2 = _merge_centered_moments(v_mean, v_m2, v_count, v)
+            v_count += len(v)
+    if sequence_count == 0 or u_count == 0 or v_count == 0:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "cannot fit relationship normalization without fitting u and v differences"
+        )
+    u_scale = np.maximum(np.sqrt(u_m2 / np.float32(u_count)), NORMALIZER_FLOOR)
+    v_scale = np.maximum(np.sqrt(v_m2 / np.float32(v_count)), NORMALIZER_FLOOR)
+    return OnlineRelationshipNormalizer(u_mean, u_scale, v_mean, v_scale, lag)
+
+
+class OnlineRelationshipState:
+    """Maintain lagged causal i1-to-i0 statistics within one sequence."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        arm: OnlineRelationshipArm,
+        lag: OnlineRelationshipLag,
+        normalizer: OnlineRelationshipNormalizer | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        _validate_arm(arm)
+        _validate_lag(lag)
+        if normalizer is not None and normalizer.lag != lag:
+            raise ValueError("relationship normalizer lag must match the stream")
+        self.arm = arm
+        self.lag = lag
+        self.normalizer = normalizer
+        self.reset()
+
+    def reset(self) -> None:
+        """Clear lagged input history and the online coefficient state."""
+        self.rows = 0
+        self.i1_history = np.zeros((self.lag, CHANNELS), dtype=np.float32)
+        self.i0_history = np.zeros((HORIZON, CHANNELS), dtype=np.float32)
+        self.u_history = np.zeros((HORIZON, CHANNELS), dtype=np.float32)
+        self.mx = np.zeros(CHANNELS, dtype=np.float32)
+        self.my = np.zeros(CHANNELS, dtype=np.float32)
+        self.variance = np.ones(CHANNELS, dtype=np.float32)
+        self.covariance = np.zeros(CHANNELS, dtype=np.float32)
+
+    def update(self, row: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+        """Return this row's 208 fields, using only matured pairs and its prefix."""
+        raw = np.asarray(row, dtype=np.float32)
+        if raw.shape != (N_FEATURES,) or not np.isfinite(raw).all():
+            raise ValueError("expected one finite 112-wide raw row")
+        current_i0 = raw[_I0_CHANNELS]
+        current_i1 = raw[_I1_CHANNELS]
+        lag_slot = self.rows % self.lag
+        u_available = self.rows >= self.lag
+        raw_u = current_i1 - self.i1_history[lag_slot] if u_available else None
+        u = (
+            self._standardize_u(raw_u)
+            if raw_u is not None
+            else np.zeros(CHANNELS, dtype=np.float32)
+        )
+        slot = self.rows % HORIZON
+        features = np.zeros(FEATURE_WIDTH, dtype=np.float32)
+        if self.rows >= HORIZON:
+            matured_v = self._standardize_v(current_i0 - self.i0_history[slot])
+            matured_u = self.u_history[slot]
+            old_slope = self._slope()
+            old_intercept = self.my - old_slope * self.mx
+            error = matured_v - (old_intercept + old_slope * matured_u)
+            if self._should_update():
+                self._update_pair(matured_u, matured_v)
+            slope = self._slope()
+            intercept = self.my - slope * self.mx
+            forecast = intercept + slope * u
+            features[:] = np.clip(
+                np.concatenate((matured_v, forecast, error, slope)),
+                -FEATURE_CLIP,
+                FEATURE_CLIP,
+            )
+        self.i0_history[slot] = current_i0
+        self.u_history[slot] = u
+        self.i1_history[lag_slot] = current_i1
+        self.rows += 1
+        return features
+
+    def transform(self, raw_rows: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+        """Process a sequence chunk while carrying state into the next chunk."""
+        sequence = _validate_sequence(raw_rows)
+        output = np.empty((len(sequence), FEATURE_WIDTH), dtype=np.float32)
+        for index, row in enumerate(sequence):
+            output[index] = self.update(row)
+        return output
+
+    def transform_compiled(self, raw_rows: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+        """Process a chunk with the strict-FP32 serial Numba kernel."""
+        from wnn.online_relationship_numba import transform_relationship_rows
+
+        sequence = _validate_sequence(raw_rows)
+        if self.normalizer is None:
+            u_mean = np.zeros(CHANNELS, dtype=np.float32)
+            u_scale = np.ones(CHANNELS, dtype=np.float32)
+            v_mean = np.zeros(CHANNELS, dtype=np.float32)
+            v_scale = np.ones(CHANNELS, dtype=np.float32)
+            normalized = False
+        else:
+            u_mean = self.normalizer.u_mean
+            u_scale = self.normalizer.u_scale
+            v_mean = self.normalizer.v_mean
+            v_scale = self.normalizer.v_scale
+            normalized = True
